propositions: Multiple bundle objects for a single ref cause clone/push failures due to ambiguous ref resolution and git-remote-s3 rejecting writes while bundles > 1, rendering the store unclonable and creating a retry deadlock.
Upstream git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() on EOF) and silently discards non-chosen heads, losing unique ticket events from an append-only store.

Rebar must heal multi-bundle state by lossless iterated 2-parent merges (reusing sync's _union_merge semantics), writing the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting originals, and never discarding any head.

The heal acquires the helper's own conditional-put S3 lock (acquire_lock/release_lock), enumerates bundles under the lock (TOCTOU guard), fetches all heads locally, merges them iteratively, puts the merged bundle, deletes originals, and releases the lock—all S3 ops routed through git_remote_s3's S3Remote/.s3 client.
At every crash point >= 1 bundle carrying the full merged history remains remotely (write merged tip before any delete, never delete merged tip), ensuring recovery is idempotent and lossless.

The heal runs inside rebar's write_lock (outer: helper S3 ref-lock; inner: write_lock) to prevent races with local commiters, and surfaces fsck-recover on unresolvable content conflicts without deleting any remote bundle.
